fichas.title: Heating surfaces and room air movement
fichas.summary: Radiator location affects room air circulation: radiators below windows intercept air cooled by the glazing, while radiators on internal walls can produce cool air near the floor and warm air near the ceiling. Surface heating in floor, ceiling, or wall areas provides uniform radiant heat at low temperatures. Convectors heat air directly and can be recessed or clad; their performance depends on recess height. The page also compares room-temperature curves and the effects of radiator covers.

fichas.title: Radiator types and standard dimensions
fichas.summary: The page describes tubular steel, steel, cast-iron, and panel radiators, with standardised cast-iron and steel radiator tables giving height, boss spacing, and depth in millimetres. Tubular radiators are available in multiple rows; panel radiators may include convector plates. Cast-iron and steel radiator dimensions are specified by DIN 4703-1.
